item.title: The Koto II experiment
item.description:
arXiv:2611.08514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $K_L ightarrow \pi^0
u ar
u$ is a golden mode for flavour physics: it is highly suppressed in the Standard Model, with a predicted branching ratio of $3 	imes 10^{-11}$ and a theoretical uncertainty of just 2\%, and is therefore extremely sensitive to new physics. The KOTO experiment at J-PARC is searching for this decay. Using the data taken in 2021, it has set the most stringent upper limit to date of $2.2 	imes 10^{-9}$ on the branching ratio at 90\% C.L. We present KOTO II, a next-generation experiment at J-PARC proposed in 2024, which aims to measure the $K_L ightarrow \pi^0
u ar
u$ branching ratio with a sensitivity below $10^{-12}$ in the 2030s.
item.dc:creator: Silvia Martellotti

item.title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.08694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.

item.title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately $30\%$, $20\%$ and $15\%$, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of $t\bar{t}$ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the $\nu\bar{\nu}$ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton $t\bar{t}$ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.
item.dc:creator: V. Aushev, M. Spitsyn, R. Yermolenko, O. Zenaiev

item.title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the azimuthal dependence of transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) in dijet events in heavy-ion collisions. In the back-to-back region this observable resolves the energy flow around $\phi=\pi$ and is sensitive to medium-induced momentum broadening and the response of the medium. To isolate final-state effects, we consider a quark-antiquark pair produced in a colour-singlet hard process and propagating through a homogeneous background medium. Starting from the vacuum TMD factorization formula, we combine NLL$'$ resummation with medium modifications at first order in the strong coupling. For the parameters studied, (classical) momentum broadening lowers the back-to-back peak and leaves the distribution elsewhere nearly unchanged, while radiative corrections significantly suppress the peak further and enhance larger angular decorrelations. We additionally include the medium response sourced by each jet, as a mean energy flow. This spreads the deposited energy over the whole azimuth, so that the contribution to the TEEC varies slowly across the back-to-back region, is small at the peak and grows toward larger angles.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Barata, Hai Tao Li, Andrey V. Sadofyev, Jo\~ao M. Silva

item.title: Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in M{\o}ller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give $\sin^2\theta_W=1/4$ at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang

item.title: Just CaloCHILL: fast hadronic shower generation in a learned latent space
item.description: arXiv:2611.08606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Calorimeter showers are the most expensive part of detector simulation, and highly granular calorimeters, in which a single hadronic shower leaves thousands of energy deposits, make them more expensive still. We present CaloCHILL (Calorimeter Hits In Learned Latents), a generative model that does not produce these deposits one by one: instead it generates a compact summary of the shower in a learned latent space and expands it to full resolution only at the end. The complete shower, including the arrival time of every hit, is built in three stages: a flow-matching model first sets the number of hits and the earliest hit time in each calorimeter layer, a mean-flow model then generates the latent summary, and the decompressor of a variational autoencoder turns it into the full point cloud, giving every hit its position, energy and time. Sparse attention along the shower axis keeps this compression affordable for showers with thousands of hits. On positive-pion showers in the calorimeter of the International Large Detector, a proposed detector for the FCC-ee, CaloCHILL reproduces the main shower observables, including their time structure. This new model is 600 times faster than its predecessor, while improving on all accuracy metrics considered.
item.dc:creator: Henry Day-Hall, Frank Gaede, Gregor Kasieczka, Katja Kr\"uger, Martina Mozzanica

item.title: Higher Order Component Attribution via Learned Surrogates in High Energy Physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.08656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Experimental High Energy Physics (HEP) has adopted the transformer architecture for identification of jets, particularly the state-of-the-art Particle Transformer (ParT) which injects explicit information about particle correlations into the attention mechanism. While able to achieve state-of-the-art results in accuracy, interpretability to its effectiveness has been limited. In this paper we propose component attribution methods using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that directly tie back to the physical descriptors of jets, to probe whether mechanisms such as Multi-Head Attention (MHA), or the ParT architecture, are able to learn these as discriminating features.
item.dc:creator: Lauri Laatu, Aritra Bal, Benedikt Maier, Markus Klute, Michael Spannowsky

item.title: Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
item.description: arXiv:2611.09095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $\eta$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leq\alpha\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.
item.dc:creator: Yue Su, Ying-Bo He, Xiao-Yun Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu

item.title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
item.description: arXiv:2611.09478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $\theta^{}_{23} = \left(\theta^{}_{12} + \theta^{}_{13}\right)/2 + \pi/8$, which predicts $\theta^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-zhong Xing

item.title: The ATAR, a dense and compact vertex detector for the PIONEER experiment
item.description: arXiv:2611.09489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: PIONEER is an approved experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland that aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons with an accuracy of 0.01%. This is an order of magnitude improvement in precision compared to its predecessors and approaches the accuracy of the standard model prediction. The key elements of PIONEER are a high resolution calorimeter built concentrically around the high granularity active target (ATAR). The ATAR is composed of a stack of 48 low gain avalanche strip detectors (LGADs) to stop the beam pions and provide detailed information of the event topology. This will include precise timing (in the order of 200ps), spatial information (to an accuracy of about 60 micro meter) and pulse height information with a high dynamic range to separate pion stops from muons and MIPs. To avoid affecting the energy measurement of the positrons, the readout electronics is placed outside the acceptance angle of the calorimeter. It is composed of a fast amplifier and a fast sampling chip digitizing the LGAD wave form for real time analysis. The paper describes the PIONEER-experiment with focus on the ATAR and its readout. The status of the development and activities in 2026 will be reported.
item.dc:creator: Tilman Rohe (Paul Scherrer Institut, Villigen, Switzerland), for the PIONEER collaboration

item.title: The PICO-40L detector
item.description: arXiv:2611.09517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The PICO collaboration has designed and constructed a novel bubble chamber to search for evidence of Weakly Interacting Massive Particles, a leading dark matter candidate. The PICO-40L detector is the successor to PICO-60, and uses a fully redesigned system for pressurization of the active volume after a bubble nucleation event. Pressure in PICO-40L is transferred to the target fluid through a set of two nested synthetic quartz vessels connected by bellows below the active volume. This is in contrast to the design of earlier detectors in which the pressure was transferred through a buffer fluid atop the target fluid, within a single synthetic quartz vessel connected to a bellows above the active volume. Removing the buffer fluid removes the potential for backgrounds arising from the interface between the two fluids, and moving the bellows below the target fluid suppresses potential backgrounds from particulates originating from the bellows. The newly designed detector concept of PICO-40L is referred to as the Right-Side-Up (RSU) design and requires a dedicated thermal system to keep the lower region of the detector cold while the upper region is stably superheated. The main goal of PICO-40L is to establish the performance characteristics of the RSU detector concept, which will inform the operating configuration of the final generation PICO dark matter detector, PICO-500, which is currently under construction at SNOLAB. This paper reviews the design, installation, and performance of the PICO-40L detector.

item.title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
item.description: arXiv:2611.09788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $\nu_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. Our factorized and nonfactorized cross sections agree, remaining 20% higher than the measured value. In addition, we use NSM single-nucleon transition densities as ansatz and find that solving the anomaly requires fine-tuned densities, with percent-level cancellations and an overall scale orders of magnitude larger than the calculated NSM ones. We conclude that the gallium anomaly is not solved when using realistic nuclear transition densities.
item.dc:creator: D. Castillo, D. Frycz, J. Men\'endez

item.title: Analytical Markov Chain for Spatiotemporal Flux Evolution of the Inner Filter Effect in Fluorescent Media
item.description: arXiv:2607.11815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characterizing emission and decay time spectra in multi-component fluorescent media is essential for identifying intrinsic material properties and optimizing detectors. However, wavelength evolution from the secondary inner filter effect (IFE) distorts these observable spectra. While Monte Carlo (MC) ray-tracing can simulate this distortion, accumulating adequate tracking statistics requires long computation times, which hinders parameter optimization within high-dimensional spaces. This paper presents an analytical Markovian transport model based on spatiotemporal decoupling. A Laplace transform converts the multi-nested convolution integrals over continuous domains into a discrete Markov transition matrix, reducing the computational complexity from an exponential scale with respect to wavelength bins $N_{\lambda}$ and cascade order $n$, $\mathcal{O}(N_{\lambda}^n)$, to a linear scale, $\mathcal{O}(N_{\lambda} + n)$. The resulting algebraic solutions evaluate transient decay time spectra as a continuum superposition of Gamma wave packets and predict steady-state wavelength spectrum distortions driven by the IFE within a sub-second timescale. Validations across orthogonal and front-face spectrometer configurations show that the calculated spectra match MC simulations in lineshape. This model can serve as a fast forward engine to accelerate parameter space screening, provide early-stage detector design references, and act as a physics-constrained input for event vertex reconstruction algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Xuhui Yang, Guofu Cao

item.title: Search for $C\!P$ violation in $D^+ \to \phi \pi^+$ decays
item.description: arXiv:2607.20276v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A search for charge-parity ($C\!P$) violation in the Cabibbo-suppressed $D^+ \to \phi \pi^+$ decay is presented, using proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $6\text{ fb}^{-1}$, collected at a centre-of-mass energy of $13\text{ TeV}$ with the LHCb detector during Run 2. An abundant sample of $D^+ \to K_{\rm S}^0 \pi^+$ decays is employed to correct for asymmetries arising from the production of the charmed meson and from detection effects associated with the charged pion accompanying the $\phi$ meson. Asymmetries induced by interference of multiple processes, such as neutral kaon mixing, regeneration of neutral kaons, and interference between the Cabibbo-favoured $D^+ \to \overline{K}^0 \pi^+$ and the doubly Cabibbo-suppressed $D^+ \to {K}^0 \pi^+$ decay, are subtracted. The direct $C\!P$ asymmetry in the $D^+ \to \phi \pi^+$ decay is measured to be \begin{equation*} a_{C\!P}(D^+ \to \phi \pi^+) = \left(0.1 \pm 4.9\text{ (stat)} \pm 2.4\text{ (syst)} \right)\times 10^{-4}. \end{equation*} For the first time at a hadron collider, the modulus of the ratio and the relative strong phase of the $D^+ \to {K}^0 \pi^+$ to $D^+ \to \overline{ K}^0 \pi^+$ decay amplitudes are also investigated. Two-dimensional confidence intervals are reported for these parameters.

item.title: A High Performance Partial Wave Analysis Framework for Hadron Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2608.25963v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial wave analysis (PWA) is a key method in hadron physics for extracting the properties of hadronic resonances. As experimental statistics grow, conventional implementations face severe difficulties in both memory usage and speed. We present \texttt{CTPWA}, a high performance PWA framework based on covariant tensor formalism. This framework adopts extensive precomputation and caching mechanisms, as well as fully GPU-based likelihood computation and minimization. With these optimization, the fitting speed is accelerated by two orders of magnitude relative to autograd-based GPU PWA programs, rendering high-statistics partial-wave analysis feasible at high-precision experiments like BESIII.
item.dc:creator: Benhou Xiang, Shuangshi Fang, Beijiang Liu

item.title: Higgs Signal Strength Estimation with Machine Learning under Systematic Uncertainties
item.description: arXiv:2509.00672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a dedicated graph neural network (GNN)-based methodology for the extraction of the Higgs boson signal strength $\mu$, incorporating systematic uncertainties. The architecture features two branches: a deterministic GNN that processes kinematic variables unaffected by nuisance parameters, and an uncertainty-aware GNN that handles inputs modulated by systematic effects through gated attention-based message passing. Their outputs are fused to produce classification scores for signal-background discrimination. During training we sample nuisance-parameter configurations and aggregate the loss across them, promoting stability of the classifier under systematic shifts and effectively decorrelating its outputs from nuisance variations. The resulting binned classifier outputs are used to construct a Poisson likelihood, which enables profile likelihood scans over signal strength, with nuisance parameters profiled out via numerical optimization. We validate this framework on the FAIR Universe Higgs Uncertainty Challenge dataset, yielding accurate estimation of signal strength $\mu$ and its 68.27\% confidence interval, achieving competitive coverage and interval widths in large-scale pseudo-experiments. Our code "Systematics-Aware Graph Estimator" (SAGE) is publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Minxuan He, Claudius Krause, Daohan Wang

item.title: Photoluminescence of resin-based solder flux residue under ultraviolet excitation from 120 nm to 310 nm
item.description: arXiv:2605.16845v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nuisance photoluminescence is a potential source of background in particle detectors that use noble liquids as target material for galactic dark matter particles and neutrinos. Liquid argon and xenon scintillate in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) wavelength range in response to particle interactions. Photoluminescent materials that absorb these photons can cause unexpected signals that may impede event reconstruction in these detectors. We illuminated residue from different types of commercial solder flux commonly used in liquid xenon detectors with ultraviolet and VUV light and measured their photoluminescence spectra and intensities. We find that all tested flux residues photoluminesce in the visible spectral region when exposed to VUV light.
item.dc:creator: Anna Hurhina, Marjolein Troost, Andreas Leonhardt, Tina R. Pollmann

item.title: Spin Femtoscopy: A Framework for Revealing Genuine Spin Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2607.00413v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spin correlations are among the most fundamental quantum observables in many-body systems, yet they remain difficult to access experimentally in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Existing spin measurements, including hyperon polarization and vector-meson spin alignment, have revealed important single-particle spin phenomena, but genuine two-particle spin correlations in the produced hadronic system remain largely unexplored. Here we propose spin femtoscopy, a framework for accessing genuine two-particle spin correlations through spin-resolved femtoscopic measurements. The key principle is that different two-particle spin configurations can give rise to different femtoscopic correlation functions because of quantum statistics and spin-dependent final-state interactions. Using $\Lambda\Lambda$ pairs as a proof of principle, we exploit the self-analyzing weak decay of $\Lambda$ hyperons to construct spin-sensitive femtoscopic correlation functions with different singlet and triplet admixtures. We show that these observables provide experimental access to the spin-state populations of the pair and allow genuine spin correlations to be separated from spin-dependent femtoscopic mixing caused by quantum statistics and final-state interactions. This work extends femtoscopy from a probe of source geometry and final-state interactions to a framework for revealing the quantum spin structure of strongly interacting matter.
item.dc:creator: Kehao Zhang, Xuan Wang, Xiaofeng Luo

item.title: Renormalon subtracted nonrelativistic QCD for heavy hadron systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.08817v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a renormalon-subtracted formulation of potential nonrelativistic QCD (pNRQCD) for precision spectroscopy of heavy hadron systems, combining variational and Green's function Monte Carlo (VMC/GFMC) methods with static two- and three-body potentials through NNLO in $\alpha_s$ (leading order in $1/m_Q$). Minimal renormalon subtraction (MRS) systematically sums leading factorially growing terms, thereby stabilizing perturbative convergence and reducing renormalization-scale dependence. We tune charm and bottom quark masses to spin-averaged $1S$ quarkonium states and predict $\Omega_{ccc}$, $\Omega_{ccb}$, $\Omega_{cbb}$, and $\Omega_{bbb}$ baryon masses, as well as QCD-stable baryons containing top quarks. NNLO MRS results undershoot lattice QCD by 125-175 MeV, a difference we attribute to contributions beyond the static perturbative potentials, including $1/m_Q$ corrections. Applying these methods to unequal-mass fully-heavy tetraquarks, we determine the critical heavy-to-light mass ratio for binding and compute binding energies across the mass-ratio landscape.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Assi, Andreas S. Kronfeld, Simon Vaiva, Michael L. Wagman

item.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
item.description: arXiv:2608.26090v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a first application of sparse-autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics. Studying a neutrino foundation model pretrained on IceCube data and fine-tuned for direction reconstruction, we identify a validated atlas of physical concepts in the model representation, using a strict validation protocol consisting of held-out tests, matched nuisance controls, and replication across independent dictionary trainings. Causal interventions show that the direction head barely draws on this atlas. Motivated by this underused information, we train an uncertainty head on the same event-level representation to predict the model's angular reconstruction error. Unlike the direction head, it depends causally on quality and brightness features from the atlas. These results suggest that mechanistic interpretability can reveal learned latent physics encoded within a model's internal representation and help design downstream tasks that exploit it.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Bonnet-Guerrini, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, Inar Timiryasov, Vincenzo Piuri

item.title: Pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ with improved perturbative QCD formalism
item.description: arXiv:2610.41078v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the pure annihilation decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ for the first time in the standard model with $S$ and $T$ representing the states of the light scalar ($1^3\!P_0$) and tensor ($1^3\!P_2$) correspondingly. Utilizing the assignment $q\bar q$ for light scalars with two-scenarios classification, we calculate the branching ratios of $B_c^+ \to ST$ with the improved perturbative QCD (iPQCD) formalism at leading order in the strong coupling $\alpha_s$. The large branching ratios around $10^{-6}$ within uncertainties in the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa-favored channels, such as $B_c^+ \to a_0(1450) a_2(1320)$, $B_c^+ \to a_0(980, 1450)^+ f_2(1270)$, $B_c^+ \to K_0^*(700, 1430) K_2^*(1430)$, and $B_c^+ \to f_0(500, 1370, 1500) a_2(1320)^+$, are obtained in the iPQCD formalism, which would be tested at the Large Hadron Collider-beauty detector in the (near) future. The relevant tests to these theoretical predictions of large branching ratios associated with typical relative ratios could provide important opportunities for understanding the QCD dynamics of the involved modes or light scalars, as well as for exploring the reliability of the iPQCD formalism. Moreover, the direct charge-parity violating asymmetries in the decay $B_c^+ \to ST$ are naturally zero, since only tree-diagram contributions are involved.
item.dc:creator: Sheng-Yu Wang, Xin Liu, Zhen-Jun Xiao

item.title: Top Spin and CP from Equivariant Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2611.05463v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Measurements of spin correlations and CP are an exciting and challenging part of the precision-LHC program. We first show how L-GATr-slim, as a Lorentz-equivariant transformer, significantly boosts the spin analyzing power for hadronic top quarks. We then show how adding a pseudoscalar channel to its architecture allows us to learn and interpret optimal observables and their CP properties. We demonstrate this for WBF-Higgs production at parton level and top pair production including detector effects.
item.dc:creator: Henning Bahl, Marco Menen, Antoine Petitjean, Tilman Plehn
